kept.reason: Swaps in ./sim-nondeterministic; folding it into the deterministic sim test changes the kept seeds and next counts that test checks.
Its seed/rerun/forget assertions are not in the promise test, which renames the promise and marks it; folding those in changes the toml and the next counts this test checks.
The plutil sample with its four task kinds; the fresh-ties test is its own echo config whose whole point is no task, so the setups conflict.
Its own truefit.toml (an unreachable fault case); the unwritable-record test makes .truefit a file, which would break this one's record checks.
Its own truefit.toml (case dirs, a non-executable stand-in); merging configs shifts stand-in indices and the cannot-run test's next message.

Its 10 has_any cases (whole-word English, any case, hyphen-joined words, CJK substring matches and non-matches) and 2 same_name asserts are checked by no other test; the other_test only runs this code on the way to a stale-model task and asserts none of these outcomes. A merge would fold a pure table into a git-repo integration test in another crate target, hiding which behaviour failed.

Its assertions (at most the bound of JVMs alive at once, more than one at once, bound+4 runs, answers in trace order) have no counterpart in the other test, and they need a stand-in java on PATH that logs liveness; the other test checks the real pinned TLC (temp dir isolation, real states/depth, broken spec), so folding the stand-in in would change what it checks.

kept_files.reason: Deep already: ~10 public items (Model, faults, run, unbacked, unreached, files, tasks, TRACES, TLC_VERSION, sha256) front ~900 lines of pinned TLC install, run under a limit, parallel accept/reject trace checks, generated trace modules and TLC output reading; callers (main, contract, promise, next, history) each use one or two. Tests cross the CLI against real TLC; unit tests only hit pure internal seams (TLC output, TLA+ values, config sections). Splitting TLC output/trace generation into modules would spread one concept, not deepen it. Removed one stale doc line.

Deep enough: callers see run (the whole contract check, real or stand-in only), faults (config validation), without_faults, version and the two record paths; behind them sit case dirs, process spawning, fault env, normalisation, comparison and the .truefit record/differ writes. Unit tests stay on internal seams (normalise, differ). The 90-day churn is features (faults, ready/needs, no_faults) plus truefit#32's move of config, host and date out of it; no pass-through or shallow piece is left to move.

kept_spans.reason: The fault for a failed write of the trace's module into the scratch directory check_trace just made: only the host fails it (disk full, temp dir removed mid-run); no fast test can make a fresh directory unwritable without injecting the filesystem, and dropping the fault would leave a panic or a lost error.
